title: Rollout velocity tuning lab notes & release dossier (Feb 2028)
body:
Context:
This is the lab notebook for experimenting with traffic velocity (softstart / ramp / throttle curves) between staging and prod for the March customer-facing release. Primary goal: reduce transient error spikes during ramp while keeping end-to-end p95 latency under 250ms for most routes. Secondary goal: capture a concise release digest that the on-call and product owners can use during the week-of deploy.

High-level summary (one-liner):
- Attempted three velocity profiles (linear, logistic, and step-hold) across two staging rings and one canary cohort; logistic ramp with short step-hold at 60% produced the best error vs latency tradeoff.

Quick deploy cadence (week-of):
- Day -2 (Tue 09:00 PT): Preflight traffic sim (local) + acceptance tests. Owner: Priya.
- Day -1 (Wed 18:00 PT): Dry-run deploy to staging-B (10% of staging traffic), smoke pass. Owner: Liam.
- Day 0 (Thu 08:00 PT): Canary rollout to 3% prod traffic, metrics baseline snapshot. Owner: Maya.
- Day 0 (Thu 09:00–13:00 PT): Velocity phase 1: ramp to 30% with logistic curve over 60 minutes, step-hold 10m. Owner: Maya + SRE.
- Day 0 (Thu 14:00–17:00 PT): Velocity phase 2: ramp to 60% with 30m smoothing, step-hold 20m. Owner: SRE lead.
- Day 0 (Thu 18:00 PT): Final ramp to 100% in two blocks (60→85, 85→100) with 10m observation windows. Owner: Release lead.
- Day +1 (Fri): Post-rollout verification window; quality regressions triage. Owner: Product QA.

Preflight checklist (must pass before any prod ramp):
- [ ] Release branch merged and build artifacts archived (GH PR #4521).
- [ ] Model version pinned in manifest + compatibility shim tested.
- [ ] Smoke tests: generation, streaming, embeddings, and function-calling (automation run, zero failures).
- [ ] Quotas & throttles configured for canary cohort (circuit breakers enabled).
- [ ] Canary alert channels pre-subscribed (pager, slack, sms).
- [ ] Telemetry snapshot captured: baseline dashboards saved, drift thresholds noted.
- [ ] Rollback playbook staged and owner assigned.

Velocity profiles tested (lab results):
- Linear ramp (0→100 over 3h):
  - Pros: predictable throughput.
  - Cons: noticeable p95 latency climb at ~45% traffic, two transient 500s events during kernel swap.
- Logistic ramp (s-curve, 0→100 over 2h with 30m inflection):
  - Pros: smoother CPU/GPU load, fewer 500s, p95 stayed <250ms in 90% of intervals.
  - Cons: slightly longer time-to-full.
- Step-hold (blocks: 0→20 hold→50 hold→100):
  - Pros: easiest to reason about for product owners, clean rollback points.
  - Cons: bursts at step edges created KV cache pressure and short latency spikes.

Recommended production profile (single-line):
- Use a hybrid: logistic ramp to 60% (90 minutes) + step-hold (20 minutes) for 60→100 split into two smaller jumps (60→80, 80→100). This balances latency and time-to-serve.

Critical observability gates (safety thresholds):
- p95 latency > 350ms sustained for 5 minutes → pause ramp and revert to previous tier.
- error rate (5xx) > 0.8% for 3 consecutive 1-minute buckets → pause ramp and investigate.
- GPU OOM/driver errors → immediate rollback.
- Model-quality drift (eval prompt set degradation > 4%) → hold and notify ML owner.

Rollout communications (slack templates):
- Canary start: /msg #release-ops Canary start: 3% at 08:00 PT. Watch p95, 5xx, and model-quality channel.
- Hold/Resume: /msg @sre "Pausing ramp at 30% due to p95 spike"; include snapshot link.
- Complete: /msg #release-ops "Rollout complete — traffic at 100%" with digest and follow-ups.

Rollback matrix (condensed):
- Trigger: sustained p95 > 350ms or 5xx > 1% → Action: rollback to previous canary snapshot; Route: redirect traffic back to prior model variant using routing policy A. Owner: SRE responder.
- Trigger: model-quality regression detected → Action: disable new model runtime and failover to baseline model endpoint. Owner: ML on-call.

Release notes (draft for product & customers):
- Short (customer-facing):
  - "March release: improved inference stability and reduced cold-start latency for complex chat flows. Available immediately; no client changes required."
- Long (internal draft):
  - "This release contains runtime changes to KV cache eviction and a new kernel selection heuristic that reduces token generation latency for multi-turn chat. The rollout will use a staged velocity profile to avoid transient spikes. See internal rollout digest for observability thresholds and contact points."

Telemetry & dashboards to monitor (links saved in Confluence artifact):
- Per-route latency (p50/p95/p99)
- 5xx rate and 4xx rate trendlines
- GPU utilization and memory pressure heatmap
- KV cache hit ratio and eviction rate
- Model eval set pass-rate (nightly canary eval)

Open questions / experiment notes (to resolve during lab):
- Does the KV cache warm-up benefit outweigh initial extra memory pressure when using step-hold at 60%? Lab indicates yes for cold requests from new users but increases short-term p95 during step edges.
- Can batching windows be tuned dynamically during ramp (adaptive batching) to smooth latency? Prototype exists but needs SLO-safe fallback.
- Should we enable circuit-breaker on LLM route X earlier (10% threshold) or only on 30%? Recommend conservative 30% for this release.

Post-rollout tasks (Day +1 to +7):
- Day +1: Run extended eval suite against live traffic sample; capture and compare to preflight baseline. Owner: ML Eng.
- Day +2: Billing and cost-sampling for token counts at nominal traffic. Owner: Finance/CostOps.
- Day +3: Retro with SRE/Product/ML — capture lessons and update the velocity playbook. Owner: Release lead.

Appendix: quick links and artifact pointers (copied into linked_artifacts):
- Confluence: RE-1824-velocity-lab (detailed charts)
- GH: PR #4521 (artifact)
- Jira: RELEASE-893 (release ticket)

Notes to self (rough):
- If we hit unexpected kernel swap failures again, escalate to infra on-call and plan an emergency low-latency fallback route that serves smaller-context requests only.
- Keep the canary window long enough to catch KV-tier blips (20m min).

End of dossier.

-- Maya (release conductor)
